column1: Many procedures are available for obtaining data about a language.
column2: 获取语言数据的方法有很多。

column1: They range from a carefully planned, intensive field investigation in a foreign country to a casual introspection about one’s mother tongue carried out in an armchair at home.
column2: 这些方法既包括在国外精心规划、深入开展的实地调查，也包括坐在家里的扶手椅上，随意想想自己的母语是怎么用的。

column1: In all cases, someone has to act as a source of language data — an informant.
column2: 无论采用哪种方法，都需要有人充当语言资料的来源，也就是语料提供者。
column3: In all cases|无论哪种情况

column1: Informants are (ideally) native speakers of a language, who provide utterances for analysis and other kinds of information about the language (e.g. translations, comments about correctness, or judgements on usage).
column2: 受访者（理想情况下）是该语言的母语者，他们提供言语样本以及关于该语言的其他信息，例如翻译、对正确性的评论或使用方式的判断。

column1: Often, when studying their mother tongue, linguists act as their own informants, judging the ambiguity, acceptability, or other properties of utterances against their own intuitions.
column2: 在研究母语时，语言学家常常自己充当信息提供者，根据自身的直觉判断语句的模糊性、可接受性及其他属性。

column1: The convenience of this approach makes it widely used, and it is considered the norm in the generative approach to linguistics.
column2: 这种方法的便利性使其被广泛采用，在生成语言学中被视为标准做法。

column1: But a linguist’s personal judgements are often uncertain, or disagree with the judgements of other linguists, at which point recourse is needed to more objective methods of enquiry, using non-linguists as informants.
column2: 但语言学家的个人判断往往不确定，或与其他语言学家的判断相悖，此时就需要采用更客观的调查方法，借助非语言学家作为信息提供者。

column1: The latter procedure is unavoidable when working on foreign languages, or child speech.
column2: 在研究外语或儿童语言时，后一种方法是不可避免的。

column1: Many factors must be considered when selecting informants — whether one is working with single speakers (a common situation when languages have not been described before), two people interacting, small groups or large-scale samples.
column2: 在选择信息提供者时，需要考虑许多因素——无论是与单个说话者进行交流（当语言尚未被描述时，这种情况很常见），还是与两人互动、小群体或大样本规模的交流。

column1: Age, sex, social background and other aspects of identity are important, as these factors are known to influence the kind of language used.
column2: 年龄、性别、社会背景等身份特征非常重要，因为这些因素会影响人们使用的语言类型。

column1: The topic of conversation and the characteristics of the social setting (e.g. the level of formality) are also highly relevant, as are the personal qualities of the informants (e.g. their fluency and consistency).
column2: 谈话的主题以及社交环境的特征（例如正式程度）也非常重要；同样重要的还有参与对话的人的个人品质，比如他们的表达流畅度与一致性。

column1: For larger studies, scrupulous attention has been paid to the sampling theory employed, and in all cases, decisions have to be made about the best investigative techniques to use.
column2: 对于规模较大的研究项目来说，对所使用的抽样方法会进行严格的评估。在所有情况下，都需要决定采用哪种最佳的调查技术。

column1: Today, researchers often tape-record informants.
column2: 如今，研究人员常使用录音设备记录受访者。

column1: This enables the linguist’s claims about the language to be checked, and provides a way of making those claims more accurate (‘difficult’pieces of speech can be listened to repeatedly).
column2: 这使得语言学家关于该语言的论述能够得到验证，同时也有助于让这些论述更加准确——因为那些‘难以理解’的语音片段可以反复聆听以进行确认。

column1: But obtaining naturalistic, good-quality data is never easy.
column2: 不过，获取自然且高质量的数据从来都不是一件容易的事。

column1: People talk abnormally when they know they are being recorded, and sound quality can be poor.
column2: 当人们知道自己正在被录音时，他们的说话方式会变得异常，而且录音的质量也可能很差。

column1: A variety of tape-recording procedures have thus been devised to minimise the ‘observer’s paradox’ (how to observe the way people behave when they are not being observed).
column2: 因此，人们设计了多种录音技术来尽量减少‘观察者悖论’的出现——即如何在没有人观察到的情况下，仍然能够记录下人们的行为表现。

column1: Some recordings are made without the speakers being aware of the fact — a procedure that obtains very natural data, though ethical objections must be anticipated.
column2: 有些录音是在扬声器并未意识到这一点的情况下进行的——这种处理方式能够获取非常自然的数据，不过还是需要考虑一些伦理问题。

column1: Alternatively, attempts can be made to make the speaker forget about the recording, such as keeping the tape recorder out of sight, or using radio microphones.
column2: 另一种方法是试图让说话人忘记录音的存在，比如将录音机藏起来，或使用无线麦克风。

column1: A useful technique is to introduce a topic that quickly involves the speaker, and stimulates a natural language style (e.g. asking older informants about how times have changed in their locality).
column2: 一个有效的技巧是引入一个能够迅速吸引说话人兴趣的话题，从而激发自然的语言表达方式（例如，可以询问年长的受访者关于他们所在地区的变化情况）。

column1: An audio tape recording does not solve all the linguist’s problems, however.
column2: 不过，录音带并不能解决语言学家面临的所有问题。

column1: Speech is often unclear and ambiguous.
column2: 口语常常模糊且含混。

column1: Where possible, therefore, the recording has to be supplemented by the observer’s written comments on the non-verbal behaviour of the participants, and about the context in general.
column2: 因此，在可能的情况下，录音应辅以观察者对参与者非语言行为以及整体情境的书面描述。

column1: A facial expression, for example, can dramatically alter the meaning of what is-said.
column2: 例如，一个面部表情就可以极大地改变所说内容的含义。

column1: Video recordings avoid these problems to a large extent, but even they have limitations (the camera cannot be everywhere), and transcriptions always benefit from any additional commentary provided by an observer.
column2: 视频记录在很大程度上避免了这些问题，但即便如此仍存在局限（摄像机无法覆盖所有区域），而转录始终能从观察者提供的额外评论中获益。

column1: Linguists also make great use of structured sessions, in which they systematically ask their informants for utterances that describe certain actions, objects or behaviour.
column2: 语言学家也广泛采用有结构的会话，系统地向受访者要求描述特定动作、物体或行为的言语表达。

column1: With a bilingual informant, or through use of an interpreter, it is possible to use translation techniques (‘How do you say table in your language?’).
column2: 借助双语受访者，或通过口译员，可以采用翻译技巧（‘你们语言里‘桌子’怎么说？’）

column1: A large number of points can be covered in a short time, using interview worksheets and questionnaires.
column2: 通过使用访谈表和问卷，可以在短时间内覆盖大量语言点。

column1: Often, the researcher wishes to obtain information about just a single variable, in which case a restricted set of questions may be used: a particular feature of pronunciation, for example, can be elicited by asking the informant to say a restricted set of words.
column2: 通常，研究人员只希望获取关于某个变量的信息，此时可使用一组有限的问题：例如，通过要求受访者说出一组特定单词，可以提取其发音特征。

column1: There are also several direct methods of elicitation, such as asking informants to fill in the blanks in a substitution frame (e.g. I ___ see a car), or feeding them the wrong stimulus for correction (‘Is it possible to say I no can see?’).
column2: 还有一些直接的信息引出方法，比如让受访者填写替换框架中的空白（如：我___看到一辆车），或提供错误刺激以供修正（如：可以说‘我不能看到’吗？）

column1: A representative sample of language, compiled for the purpose of linguistic analysis, is known as a corpus.
column2: 用于语言学分析的代表性语言样本被称为语料库。

column1: A corpus enables the linguist to make unbiased statements about frequency of usage, and it provides accessible data for the use of different researchers.
column2: 语料库使语言学家能够做出无偏见的使用频率判断，并为不同研究人员提供可获取的数据。

column1: Its range and size are variable.
column2: 其范围和大小是可变的。

column1: Some corpora attempt to cover the language as a whole, taking extracts from many kinds of text; others are extremely selective, providing a collection of material that deals only with a particular linguistic feature.
column2: 有些语料库试图全面涵盖语言整体，从多种文本中提取样本；另一些则极为选择性，仅提供专门针对某一语言特征的材料。

column1: The size of the corpus depends on practical factors, such as the time available to collect, process and store the data: it can take up to several hours to provide an accurate transcription of a few minutes of speech.
column2: 语料库的规模取决于实际因素，比如可用于收集、处理和存储数据的时间：对几分钟的语音进行准确转录可能需要数小时。

column1: Sometimes a small sample of data will be enough to decide a linguistic hypothesis; by contrast, corpora in major research projects can total millions of words.
column2: 有时候，一小部分数据就足以支持某个语言假设；而大型研究项目中的语料库则可能包含数百万个单词。

column1: An important principle is that all corpora, whatever their size, are inevitably limited in their coverage, and always need to be supplemented by data derived from the intuitions of native speakers of the language, through either introspection or experimentation.
column2: 一个重要的原则是：无论语料库规模多大，其覆盖范围都不可避免地有限，必须依靠母语者的直觉，通过内省或实验来补充数据。
